name: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme
nodalDept: Department Of Empowerment Of Persons With Disabilities
briefDescription: Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme provides health insurance of up to ₹1 lakh per annum to persons with disabilities covered under the National Trust Act — covering OPD, surgery, hospitalisation, alternative medicines and preventive care — at a premium of ₹250–₹500/year.
descriptionMd:
Niramaya Health Insurance Scheme, run by the National Trust (Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities, MoSJ&E), provides affordable health coverage to persons with disabilities that are notified under the National Trust Act, 1999 — specifically Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation (Intellectual Disability), and Multiple Disabilities.

The scheme is implemented through tie-ups with insurance companies and Registered Organisations (ROs) of the National Trust. Premiums are heavily subsidised by the National Trust — a person from a BPL family pays just ₹250/year for ₹1 lakh coverage.
benefitsMd:
- **Health insurance cover of up to ₹1,00,000 per year** per beneficiary.
- Coverage includes:
  - OPD treatment — medicines, pathology and diagnostic tests
  - Surgery and specialist consultation
  - Hospitalisation expenses
  - Alternative medicine (AYUSH)
  - Preventive health check-ups for non-ailing members
  - Corrective surgery and therapy
  - Non-surgical/dental treatment
  - Physiotherapy and speech therapy
- **Annual premium:**
  - BPL families: **₹250/year**
  - Others: **₹500/year**
  - The National Trust pays the remaining actuarial premium as subsidy.
eligibilityMd:
- Must have **at least one of the four disabilities** covered under the [National Trust Act, 1999](https://thenationaltrust.gov.in/): Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation/Intellectual Disability, or Multiple Disabilities.
- Must hold a **valid disability certificate** from a competent authority.
- No age bar — covers persons of all ages.
- Both BPL and non-BPL families are eligible (premium differs).
exclusionsMd:
- Disabilities **not listed** under the National Trust Act 1999 (such as locomotor disability, deafness, blindness alone) are **not covered** under this specific scheme — they may be covered by other schemes.
- Pre-existing conditions **are** covered, but there is a waiting period for certain treatments as per the insurer's terms.
applicationMd:
**Step 1:** Locate the nearest **Registered Organisation (RO)** of the National Trust in your area — the list is at [thenationaltrust.gov.in](https://thenationaltrust.gov.in/content/registered_organization.php).
**Step 2:** Visit the RO with the person with disability and their guardian (if any).
**Step 3:** Submit the application form along with: disability certificate, Aadhaar, income/BPL certificate (for BPL premium), photograph.
**Step 4:** Pay the annual premium (₹250 for BPL / ₹500 for others) at the RO.
**Step 5:** The RO enrolls the beneficiary; an **insurance card** is issued for use at empanelled hospitals for cashless treatment.
